body.translated_text: Homage to the Omniscient One!

children.translated_text: Together with these and many other hundreds of thousands of myriads of <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons). ||1||

body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks — twelve hundred and fifty monks — all recognized as possessing superknowledges, elders, great disciples, all of them <s>Arhats</s>. Namely: the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>, <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, <s>Revata</s>, <s>Śuddhipanthaka</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Rāhula</s>, <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Kālodayin</s>, <s>Vakkula</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s> — along with these and many other great disciples, and also with many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Namely: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Kumārabhūta, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ajita</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Gandhahasti</s> (Fragrant Elephant), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Nityodyukta</s> (Ever-Exerting), and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s> (Never-Resting) — along with these and many other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, and also with <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, and <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>.

children.text: nāsti sattvānāṃ kāyaduḥkhaṃ na cittaduḥkhaṃ apramāṇāny eva sukhakāraṇāni /
children.translated_text: there is no bodily suffering for beings, nor mental suffering — the causes of happiness are immeasurable.

children.text: tena kāraṇena sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatīty ucyate //2//
children.translated_text: For that reason, that world-realm is called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). ||2||

body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "There exists, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the western direction, beyond a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>Buddha</s>-fields from here, a world-realm called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). There, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, presently abides, lives, and continues, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s> — for what reason is that world-realm called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss)? Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>,

punar aparaṃ śāriputra sukhāvatī lokadhātuḥ saptabhir vedikābhiḥ
saptabhis tālapaṃktibhiḥ kiṃkiṇījālaiś ca samalaṃkṛtā samaṃtato 'nuparikṣiptā
citrā darśanīyā caturṇāṃ ratnānāṃ / tadyathā suvarṇasya
rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya / evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ

children.translated_text: that <s>Buddha</s>-field is adorned. ||3||

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> is adorned with seven rows of railings, seven rows of palm trees, and nets of tinkling bells, completely encircled all around — beautiful and splendid to behold — made of four precious substances: namely, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and crystal. With such splendid adornments of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>,

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> there are lotus pools made of seven precious substances: namely, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, crystal, red pearl, emerald (<s>aśmagarbha</s>), and <s>musāragalva</s> as the seventh gem. They are filled to the brim with water endowed with eight qualities, level at the banks, [shallow enough for] a crow to drink from, and strewn with golden sand. In those lotus pools, on all four sides, there are four flights of stairs — beautiful and splendid to behold — made of four precious substances: namely, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal. Around those lotus pools grow jewel-trees — beautiful and splendid to behold — made of seven precious substances: namely, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, crystal, red pearl, emerald, and <s>musāragalva</s> as the seventh gem. In those lotus pools, lotuses have grown: blue ones — blue in color, blue in radiance, blue in appearance; yellow ones — yellow in color, yellow in radiance, yellow in appearance; red ones — red in color, red in radiance, red in appearance; white ones — white in color, white in radiance, white in appearance; and variegated ones — variegated in color, variegated in radiance, variegated in appearance — as large in circumference as a cart-wheel. With such splendid adornments of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>,

body.text:
punar aparaṃ śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre nityapravāditāni divyāni
tūryāṇi suvarṇavarṇā ca mahāpṛthivī ramaṇīyā / tatra ca buddhakṣetre
triṣkṛtvo rātrau triṣkṛtvo divasasya puṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣati divyānāṃ
māṃdāravapuṣpāṇāṃ / tatra ye sattvā upapannās ta ekena purobhaktena
koṭiśatasahasraṃ buddhānāṃ vaṃdaṃty anyāṃl lokadhātūn gatvā / ekaikaṃ ca
tathāgataṃ koṭiśatasahasrābhiḥ puṣpavṛṣṭibhir abhyavakīrya punar api
tām eva lokadhātum āgacchaṃti divāvihārāya / evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra

children.translated_text: that buddha-field is adorned with the array of qualities of the buddha-field. //5//

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), divine musical instruments are constantly played, and the great earth is golden-colored and delightful. In that buddha-field, three times during the night and three times during the day, a rain of divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers falls. The beings born there, in a single morning meal-time, go to other world-systems and pay homage to a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) <s>Buddhas</s>. Having showered each <s>Tathāgata</s> with a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s> rains of flowers, they return again to that very world-system for their daytime rest. With such qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>,

body.text:
punar aparaṃ śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre saṃti haṃsāḥ kraiṃcā mayūrāś ca /
te triṣkṛtvo rātrau triṣkṛtvo divasasya saṃnipatya saṃgītiṃ kurvaṃti
sma svakasvakāni ca rutāni pravyāharaṃti / teṣāṃ pravyāharatām
iṃdriyabalabodhyaṃgaśabdo niścarati / tatra teṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ taṃ śabdaṃ
śrutvā buddhamanasikāra utpadyate dharmamanasikāra utpadyate saṃghamanasikāra
utpadyate // tat kiṃ manyase śāriputra tiryagyonigatās te
P--O.95:J.200
sattvāḥ / na punar evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / nāmāpi śāriputra
tatra buddhakṣetre nirayāṇāṃ nāsti tiryagyonīnāṃ yamalokasya
nāsti / te punaḥ pakṣisaṃghās tenāmitāyuṣā tathāgatena nirmitā
dharmaśabdaṃ niścārayaṃti / evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ

children.translated_text: That buddha-field is adorned. //6//

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that buddha-field there are swans, herons, and peacocks. Three times during the night and three times during the day, they gather together and perform a chorus, each uttering its own call. From their utterances, the sound of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), and <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) issues forth. When those people there hear that sound, mindfulness of the <s>Buddha</s> arises in them, mindfulness of the <s>Dharma</s> arises in them, mindfulness of the <s>Saṅgha</s> arises in them. Now what do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s> — are those beings born in the animal realm? This should not be viewed thus. For what reason? In that buddha-field, <s>Śāriputra</s>, not even the name of the hells exists, nor of the animal realm, nor of <s>Yama</s>'s world. Rather, those flocks of birds were created by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, and they produce the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>. With such qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that buddha-field is adorned with the array of qualities of the buddha-field.

body.text:
punar aparaṃ śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre tāsāṃ ca tālapaṃktīnāṃ teṣāṃ ca
kiṃkiṇījālānāṃ vāteritānāṃ valgur manojñaḥ śabdo niścarati /
tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra koṭiśatasahasrāṃgikasya divyasya tūryasya
cāryaiḥ(2) saṃpravāditasya valgur manojñaḥ śabdo niścarati evam eva
śāriputra tāsāṃ ca tālapaṃktīnāṃ teṣāṃ ca kiṃkiṇījālānāṃ
vāteritānāṃ valgur manojñaḥ śabdo niścarati / tatra teṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ
taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā buddhānusmṛtiḥ kāye saṃtiṣṭhati dharmānusmṛtiḥ kāye
saṃtiṣṭhati saṃghānusmṛtiḥ kāye saṃtiṣṭhati / evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra

children.translated_text: that buddha-field is adorned with the array of qualities of the buddha-field. //7//

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that buddha-field, from those rows of palm trees and those nets of bells stirred by the wind, a sweet and pleasing sound issues forth. Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, from a divine musical instrument of a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s> parts, when played by skilled musicians, a sweet and pleasing sound issues forth — even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, from those rows of palm trees and those nets of bells stirred by the wind, a sweet and pleasing sound issues forth. When those people there hear that sound, <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the Buddha) is established in their bodies, <s>dharmānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the Dharma) is established in their bodies, <s>saṅghānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the Saṅgha) is established in their bodies. With such qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>,

body.text:
tat kiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitāyur nāmocyate /
tasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra tathāgatasya teṣāṃ ca manuṣyāṇām(3)
aparimitam āyuḥpramāṇaṃ / tena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitāyur nāmocyate /
tasya ca śāriputra tathāgatasya daśa kalpā anuttarāṃ

children.translated_text: perfect and complete awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). //8//

body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s> — for what reason is that <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Amitāyus</s> (Immeasurable Life)? Indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the lifespan of that <s>Tathāgata</s> and of those beings is immeasurable. For that reason, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitāyus</s>. And, <s>Śāriputra</s>, ten <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) have passed since that <s>Tathāgata</s> attained unsurpassed

body.text:
tat kiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitābho
nāmocyate / tasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra tathāgatasyābhāpratihatā
sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu / tena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitābho nāmocyate //
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s> — for what reason is that <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Amitābha</s> (Immeasurable Light)? Indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the radiance of that <s>Tathāgata</s> is unobstructed in all buddha-fields. For that reason, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitābha</s>.

body.text:
P--O.96:J.202
tasya ca śāriputra tathāgatasyāprameyaḥ śrāvakasaṃgho yeṣāṃ na sukaraṃ
pramāṇam ākhyātuṃ śuddhānām arhatāṃ / evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra
buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ

children.translated_text: That buddha-field is adorned. //9//

body.translated_text: And, <s>Śāriputra</s>, of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>śrāvakasaṅgha</s> (assembly of disciples) is immeasurable — it is not easy to declare the number of those pure <s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones). With such qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that buddha-field is adorned with the array of qualities of the buddha-field.

body.text:
punar aparaṃ śāriputra ye 'mitāyuṣas tathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sattvā
upapannāḥ śuddhā bodhisattvā avinivartanīyā ekajātipratibaddhās

children.text: teṣāṃ śāriputra bodhisattvānāṃ na sukaraṃ pramāṇam ākhyātum
children.translated_text: The number of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not easy to declare;
they can only be described as immeasurable and innumerable,

children.text: iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchaṃti // tatra khalu punaḥ śāriputra
children.translated_text: belonging to that category of numbers. Now then, <s>Śāriputra</s>,

children.translated_text: the aspiration should be made by beings [to be reborn] in that <s>Buddha</s>-field. For what reason? Because there one comes to be in the company of such excellent persons. Not by a small root of merit, <s>Śāriputra</s>, do beings come to be reborn in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>. Whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Śāriputra</s>, shall hear the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, and having heard it shall bear it in mind — for one night, or two nights, or three nights, or four nights, or five nights, or six nights, or seven nights — shall bear it in mind with an undistracted mind: when that son of good family or daughter of good family comes to die, then, as he is dying, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, surrounded by an assembly of disciples and honored by a host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, will stand before him, and he will die with a mind unconfused. Having died, he will be reborn in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of that very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, in the world-sphere <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. Therefore then, <s>Śāriputra</s>, perceiving this compelling reason, I speak thus: respectfully should the aspiration of mind be made by a son of good family or a daughter of good family toward that <s>Buddha</s>-field —
the aspiration of mind should be made [toward rebirth there]. //10//

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the beings who have been born in the buddha-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> are all pure <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, non-retrogressing (<s>avinivartanīya</s>), bound by a single birth [to awakening].

body.translated_text: What do you think, O <s>Śāriputra</s>: for what reason is this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called 'Protected by All <s>Buddhas</s>'? Whatever sons or daughters of good family, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, will hear the name of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse and will retain the names of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones — all of them will be protected by the <s>Buddhas</s> and will become non-retrogressing (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) from unsurpassed, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, have faith, believe, and do not doubt — [this is the word] of me and of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones. Whatever sons or daughters of good family, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, will direct their minds in aspiration (<s>cittapraṇidhāna</s>) toward the <s>Buddha</s>-field of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> (of Immeasurable Life), or have directed, or are directing [their minds] — all of them will become non-retrogressing from unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and will be reborn, have been reborn, or are being reborn in that <s>Buddha</s>-field. Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, faithful sons and daughters of good family should generate the aspiration of mind toward that <s>Buddha</s>-field.

body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, I now proclaim these inconceivable virtues of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, even so, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones proclaim my inconceivable virtues: 'A most difficult thing has been accomplished by the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Supreme King of the <s>Śākyas</s>. Having attained unsurpassed, perfect awakening in the world-realm <s>Sahā</s>, he has taught a <s>Dharma</s> that is incredible to the whole world

(19)
